title: The Hound of the Baskervilles

evidence.note: The film was released in 1939, so it is not public domain by term. Public domain would need a missing notice or a missing renewal. I could not load the Stanford renewal database or the Catalog of Copyright Entries renewal volumes in this session, so no renewal check was done. A web search only turned up unsourced 'public domain' labels, which are not evidence.
This is a sound film from 1939. The recorded track would normally share the film's own copyright status, which is unresolved (see the print layer). I did not confirm any separate music rights.

The source novel by Arthur Conan Doyle was serialized in 1901-1902. Project Gutenberg lists it as public domain in the USA. The underlying story is free, but the 1939 film's own screenplay and added material are not covered by this layer.

editorial:
The Hound of the Baskervilles (1939) was made by Twentieth Century-Fox and directed by Sidney Lanfield. Basil Rathbone plays Sherlock Holmes and Nigel Bruce plays Dr. Watson. It is based on Arthur Conan Doyle's novel, which ran as a serial in 1901-1902. A creator would want it for the Rathbone and Bruce pairing and for its gothic Dartmoor mystery.

The novel is free in the US, but the film is a separate 1939 work with its own copyright. I found no verified evidence that it lapsed, and I could not check whether it was renewed in the 1966-1968 window. Some sites and uploaders label copies 'public domain' without citing a record, so that label should not be relied on. One Internet Archive upload carries a Creative Commons BY-NC-ND tag, but that is the uploader's own label and does not settle who owns the film. Before reusing footage, search the renewal records yourself.
faq: Can I reuse footage from the 1939 Hound of the Baskervilles?

Not safely yet. The Doyle novel it adapts is public domain, but the 1939 film is a separate work. I could not confirm whether it was renewed, so check the Stanford renewal database and the Copyright Office records first.
Can I make my own Hound of the Baskervilles adaptation?

Yes, from the Doyle novel. The novel was serialized in 1901-1902 and is listed as public domain in the USA. Do not copy the 1939 film's screenplay, dialogue changes or other added material unless that film is cleared.
